questions.question: Which national park in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is home to species like Megapode, crab-eating Macaque, Nicobar Pigeon, and Giant Robber Crab?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Campbell Bay National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Campbell Bay National Park** is located on the Great Nicobar Island, which is part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• The park is known for its rich biodiversity and is home to unique species such as the Megapode, crab-eating Macaque, Nicobar Pigeon, and Giant Robber Crab.
 
• It covers an area of approximately 426 square kilometers, making it one of the largest national parks in the region.
 
• The park's diverse ecosystems include tropical evergreen forests, mangroves, and coastal habitats, which provide a sanctuary for various flora and fauna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Megapode**

 
 
• The Megapode is a unique bird found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• It is known for its distinctive nesting behavior, where it builds large mounds of earth and vegetation to incubate its eggs.
 
• The heat generated from the decomposing vegetation within the mound provides the necessary warmth for the eggs to hatch.
 
 
 
• **Crab-eating Macaque**
 
 
• The crab-eating Macaque, also known as the long-tailed Macaque, is a primate species native to Southeast Asia.
 
• It is called the crab-eating Macaque because of its diet, which includes crabs, fruits, and small animals.
 
• These Macaques are known for their adaptability and can thrive in various habitats, including coastal regions and forests.
 
 
 
• **Nicobar Pigeon**
 
 
• The Nicobar Pigeon is a large, colorful bird found in the Nicobar Islands and other parts of Southeast Asia.
 
• It is known for its iridescent plumage, which displays a range of metallic colors.
 
• The Nicobar Pigeon is the closest living relative of the extinct dodo bird.
 
 
 
• **Giant Robber Crab**
 
 
• The Giant Robber Crab, also known as the coconut crab, is the largest terrestrial arthropod in the world.
 
• It is known for its ability to climb trees and crack open coconuts with its powerful claws.
 
• The crab is primarily nocturnal and is found in coastal regions and forests of the Indo-Pacific islands.

questions.question: In which state of India is the Tadoba National Park located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tadoba National Park** is located in the Chandrapur district of Maharashtra.
 
• It is also known as **Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve**, which is the largest and oldest national park in Maharashtra.
 
• The park was established in 1955 and covers an area of approximately **1,727 square kilometers**.
 
• Tadoba National Park is famous for its significant population of **Bengal tigers** and is a prominent destination for wildlife enthusiasts and photographers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Parks in India**

 
 
• National parks are protected areas established by the government for the conservation of wildlife and biodiversity.
 
• India is home to a diverse range of national parks, each offering unique habitats and species.
 
• Some other famous national parks in India include Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand, Kaziranga National Park in Assam, and Ranthambore National Park in Rajasthan.
 
• These parks play a crucial role in the conservation of endangered species and serve as important research and education centers.
 
 
 
• **Tiger Reserves in India**
 
 
• India is home to more than 50 tiger reserves, which are established under the Project Tiger initiative launched in 1973.
 
• Tiger reserves aim to protect and increase the population of Bengal tigers in the country.
 
• These reserves provide a safe habitat for tigers and other wildlife, while also promoting eco-tourism and community involvement in conservation efforts.
 
• The Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve is one of the most popular and successful tiger reserves in India.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity in Maharashtra**
 
 
• Maharashtra is a state with rich biodiversity, encompassing various ecosystems such as forests, grasslands, and coastal regions.
 
• The state is home to several national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and conservation reserves.
 
• In addition to Tadoba National Park, other notable protected areas in Maharashtra include Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Navegaon National Park, and Melghat Tiger Reserve.
 
• The state's diverse flora and fauna contribute to its ecological significance and attract nature enthusiasts from around the world.

questions.question: Which is the natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gir Forest**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gir Forest** is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion in India.
 
• Located in the state of Gujarat, the Gir Forest National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary is home to the last remaining population of Asiatic Lions.
 
• The Asiatic Lion, also known as **Panthera leo persica**, once roamed from the Middle East to India, but now they are confined to this single location due to habitat loss and hunting.
 
• Conservation efforts in the Gir Forest have been crucial in increasing the population of these lions from the brink of extinction.
 
• The Gir Forest covers an area of approximately **1,412 square kilometers** and comprises diverse flora and fauna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Gir National Park** was established in 1965 and has since been a protected area for wildlife conservation.
 
• The Government of Gujarat and various wildlife organizations have implemented several measures to protect and increase the population of Asiatic Lions.
 
• Tourism in the Gir Forest is regulated to ensure minimal disturbance to the wildlife and their natural habitat.
 
• The Asiatic Lion differs from its African counterpart by being slightly smaller with a less developed mane.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to explore potential sites for reintroducing the Asiatic Lion to reduce the risk of the entire population being confined to a single area.

• This project aims to stem the dwindling population of the big cats and work to increase their numbers.

• Reduce factors that lead to the depletion of tiger habitats and mitigate them by suitable management.
 
• The harms done to the natural surroundings will be corrected to encourage the recuperation of the biological system to the greatest conceivable extent.
 
• Ensure a viable tiger population for **economic, scientific, cultural, aesthetic, and ecological values.**
 
• The tracking system** M-STrIPES** turned into advanced to help patrol and defend tiger habitats. It maps patrol routes and permits woodland guards to go into sightings, occasions and adjustments whilst patrolling. questions.question: In which of the following protected areas in India the human interference is prohibited?

• **National Park **is a protected area reserved for the protection of only animals, where no human intervention is allowed in any form of timber harvesting, the collection of minor forest products and private property rights; whereas a wildlife sanctuary is a protected area reserved for the conservation of only animals and human activities such as timber harvesting, the collection of minor forestry.
 
• eg. **Recently Dehing Patkai wildlife sanctuary is upgraded to a National Park so that more restriction comes and the coal mining activities gets stop.While a limited number of human activities are allowed in wildlife sanctuaries, national parks are strictly off-limits.**
 
• The Protected Areas (PAs) in India, consisting of national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and conservation and community reserves, cover about 4.89% of the geographical area of the country as of July 2016.
 
• There are currently a maximum number of national parks on the **Madhya Pradesh(Ten) and Andaman and Nicobar Islands (nine ), followed by Kerala, Maharashtra and Uttarakhand and West Bengal (six each). **
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands have the highest number of wildlife sanctuaries (96), followed by Maharashtra (41) and Tamil Nadu (29). Areas of great geological, floral, faunal or natural importance are national parks and sanctuaries.
 
• **Under the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** & its amendments, **the Indian Forest Act of 1927, the Forest (Protection) Act of 1980**, the **Biological Diversity Act, 2002 **and the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, they are notified by the State Governments and protected by the Forest Departments.
 
• In protected areas, hunting of wild animals, habitat invasion and/or degradation, construction of tourist lodges and other such practises are prohibited.

The correct answer is__** Little Rann of Kutch.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary**, sometimes referred to as the **Wild Ass Wildlife Sanctuary**, is situated in** India's Gujarat state in the Little Rann of Kutch.**
 
• The** Wildlife Protection Act of 1972** was the** legal basis** on which the** wildlife sanctuary was created.**
 
• The sanctuary is where it is possible to see the** critically endangered Indian Wild Ass (Khur)** subspecies of the **Asiatic Wild Ass species Onager (Equus hemionus).**
 
• The** main threat** faced by the sanctuary is the** illegal salt** panning activity in the area.
 
• **25% of India’s salt supply **comes from panning activity in the area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sunderbans:**

 
 
• The Sundarbans is of universal importance for** endangered species** including the** Royal Bengal Tiger, Ganges and Irawadi dolphins, estuarine crocodiles.**
 
 
 
• **Upper Himalayas:**
 
 
• The Himalayan Range's tallest mountains are known as the Great Himalayas, Greater Himalayas, or Himadri.
 
• The Greater Himalayas mountain range includes** Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, **as well as other "nearest highest" peaks like** Kangchenjunga, Lhotse, and Nanga Parbat.**
 
 
 
• **Plains of Ganga:**
 
 
• Large floodplains of the **Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra** river systems are collectively referred to as the Indus-Ganga plains, commonly referred to as the** "Great Plains."**

questions.question: Under which of the following Articles can a person directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of his Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution provides the right to individuals to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar referred to Article 32 as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution, emphasizing its importance in upholding fundamental rights.
 
• Article 32 guarantees the right to constitutional remedies, empowering the Supreme Court to issue writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari for the enforcement of these rights.
 
• This provision ensures that the fundamental rights are not merely theoretical but can be practically enforced through the highest court in India.
 
• Any individual whose fundamental rights are violated can directly approach the Supreme Court without having to go through lower courts first.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**

 
 
• These are a set of rights granted to all citizens by the Indian Constitution, aimed at ensuring individual liberty and equality.
 
• There are six fundamental rights: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
 
 
• **Writs**
 
 
• Habeas Corpus: A writ requiring a person to be brought before a judge or court, especially to secure the person's release unless lawful grounds are shown for their detention.
 
• Mandamus: A writ issued as a command to an inferior court or ordering a person to perform a public or statutory duty.
 
• Prohibition: A writ directing a subordinate to stop doing something the law prohibits.
 
• Quo Warranto: A writ requiring a person to show by what warrant an office or franchise is held, claimed, or exercised.
 
• Certiorari: A writ by which a higher court reviews a case tried in a lower court.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review**
 
 
• The power of the judiciary to review and determine the validity of a law or an order.
 
• It helps in upholding the supremacy of the Constitution and ensuring the protection of fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of India**
 
 
• The apex judicial body in India, established in 1950.
 
• It has the power to interpret the Constitution and enforce the fundamental rights of citizens.
 
• The decisions of the Supreme Court are binding on all courts within India.

questions.question: The Nagarhole National Park is located in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Karnataka__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nagarhole National Park** is a national park located in **Kodagu district** **and Mysore district** **in Karnataka, India.**
 
• It is one of **India's premier Tiger Reserves** along with the adjoining **Bandipur Tiger Reserve and Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary.**
 
• This park was declared the **thirty-sevenths Project Tiger**, **Tiger reserves of India in 1999**.
 
• It is part of the **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Corbett National Park located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jim Corbett National Park**, which is a part of the **larger Corbett Tiger Reserve,** a **Project Tiger Reserve **lies in the** Nainital district** of** Uttarakhand**.
 
• On **8th August 1936**, **India’s first national park** was **established as Hailey National Park**.
 
 
• It was named after the **then Governor of the United Provinces, British India, Sir Malcolm Hailey**.
 
 
 
• **It is also Asia’s first national park**.
 
• It was renamed **Ramganga National Park in 1954-55** and again renamed **Corbett National Park in 1955-56**.
 
• When the Government of India launched **Project Tiger in 1973**, the park became a part of this project.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
